Package com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest

Class DecodedJwt

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.http.rest.DecodedJwt
public final class DecodedJwt extends Object
The decoded, unverified contents of a JSON Web Token as produced by JwtDecoder. This is an inspection view only: the signature segment is preserved verbatim but is never checked, so nothing here implies the token is authentic, untampered, or issued by a trusted party. Treat every field as attacker-controlled until validated elsewhere.

The header and payload are exposed both as their raw JSON text (headerJson(), payloadJson()) and through typed accessors for the registered header parameters (alg, typ, kid) and the registered RFC 7519 claims. Any other claim can be read as text via claim(String).

The exp, iat and nbf claims are interpreted as NumericDate values — seconds elapsed since the UNIX epoch, UTC — and surfaced as Instants. A missing time claim yields null from its accessor.

    • headerJson

      public String headerJson()
      The Base64URL-decoded header as its original JSON text.

    • payloadJson

      public String payloadJson()
      The Base64URL-decoded payload as its original JSON text.

    • signature

      public String signature()
      The third JWT segment exactly as it appeared in the compact serialization: the Base64URL (unpadded) signature string. It is returned untouched and is never verified; for an unsecured JWS (alg = none) this is the empty string.

    • signatureBytes

      public byte[] signatureBytes()
      The raw signature bytes obtained by Base64URL-decoding signature(). These are handed back purely so a caller can display or fingerprint them; decoding them does not, and is not meant to, validate anything. Empty for an unsecured JWS.

    • audience

      public String audience()
      The aud (audience) claim, or null. Per RFC 7519 the audience may be a single string or an array of strings; when it is an array the elements are joined with ", " for this convenience accessor.

    • expiration

      The exp (expiration time) claim as an Instant, or null if absent.

    • jwtId

      public String jwtId()

    • claim

      public String claim(String name)
      The named payload claim rendered as text, or null if the claim is absent (or present but JSON null). Scalar claims — strings, numbers, booleans — are returned in their canonical text form; structured claims (objects and arrays) return null here, so use payloadJson() to inspect those.

    • isExpired

      public boolean isExpired(Instant now)
      Whether the token is expired relative to now: true when an exp claim is present and now is at or after it. Returns false when exp is absent. No clock-skew leeway is applied — the comparison is exact; add tolerance yourself if needed. This checks only the timestamp, never the signature.

    • isNotYetValid

      public boolean isNotYetValid(Instant now)
      Whether the token is not yet valid relative to now: true when an nbf claim is present and now is strictly before it. Returns false when nbf is absent. No clock-skew leeway is applied. This checks only the timestamp, never the signature.
